Incorporating the Beige Book prepared February 24, 2025 (Minneapolis Fed), the policy read remains mildly positive but more cautious. The FOMC held the target range at 4-1/4 to 4-1/2 percent and slowed QT by cutting the Treasury redemption cap to $5B, a modestly dovish balance sheet shift tempered by Governor Waller’s dissent favoring a faster runoff. The Beige Book notes slight-to-modest growth across districts, mixed consumer spending, generally flat manufacturing, and ongoing weakness in CRE—especially office. Labor markets are solid but gradually easing, with moderating wage pressures; prices continue to rise at a modest pace but remain above the 2% objective. Credit conditions are tight, loan demand is soft, and banks report rising concerns about delinquencies—consistent with SLOOS. Netting these, slower QT offers a small liquidity tailwind, but persistent credit headwinds and uneven demand argue for caution.

Adjusted take: Mildly positive, further moderated by Beige Book evidence of tight credit and uneven activity.
